title: Decode an HRESULT
description:
Take an HRESULT apart the way its documentation describes.

```
0x80070005 -> failure, facility 7 (WIN32), code 5 (access denied)
0x00000000 -> success (S_OK)
0x8007000E -> failure, facility 7 (WIN32), code 14 (out of memory)
```
hints: `FAILED(hr)` is simply `hr < 0`, because bit 31 is the sign bit of a 32-bit signed value (lesson 3.03).
The facility is `(hr >> 16) & 0x7FF` and the code `hr & 0xFFFF`.
requirements: Bit 31 is the severity, bits 16 to 26 the facility, bits 0 to 15 the code.
Write `succeeded(hr)` and `failed(hr)` the way the `SUCCEEDED` and `FAILED` macros work.
A small table of a few facilities and codes for the names.
stretch: Turn a Win32 error code into an HRESULT the way `HRESULT_FROM_WIN32` does.
